entry.strongs: H3917. Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified. Akkadian cognate lilītu: CAD L, s.v. lilītu (recalled, page not checked).
entry.partOfSpeech: noun, feminine singular; hapax legomenon in the Hebrew Bible
entry.literal: a lilith, a female demon of the lilû class (popularly heard as 'the one of the night', from layil 'night')
entry.standardEnglish: the night-monster (ASV; JPS 1917, checked 2026-11-26); the lilith, with note 'A kind of demon' (NJPS, checked 2026-11-26); the screech owl (KJV, checked); Lilith (NRSV, not verified); the night hag (RSV, recalled)
entry.wohChoice: 'the night-monster' at 34:14, a class noun with the article and in lower case, with the feminine verbs kept ('there the night-monster shall settle, and shall find for herself a place of rest'). The capitalised personal name 'Lilith' and the animal reading 'screech owl' are recorded in commentary and not used in the line. PENDING FOUNDER RULING, staged alternative: NJPS 'the lilith' (lower-case class noun, following the Akkadian–Sumerian philology), line 'yes, there the lilith shall settle, and shall find for herself a place of rest.'; if adopted, this wohChoice becomes 'the lilith' and the 34:14 line and note change with it.
entry.rationale: lîlîṯ occurs once in the Hebrew Bible, among the creatures that occupy ruined Edom. It is the Akkadian lilītu, a female demon of the lilû class, beside the masculine lilû and the ardat-lilî (CAD L, recalled); the class name is usually traced to Sumerian líl 'wind, breath', and in Hebrew the word was heard as if it came from layil 'night'. The ASV and JPS 1917 rendering 'the night-monster' reflects the Hebrew hearing of the word as a creature of the night (layil) and is the public-domain baseline; it does not follow the Akkadian–Sumerian philology, in which the class name goes back to líl 'wind, breath', though it does keep the word a class of demon. NJPS 'the lilith', with its note 'A kind of demon', is the alternative that follows the philology: it keeps the class noun in lower case without importing either the 'night' association or the personal name, and it is staged in the wohChoice pending the founder's ruling. The capitalised 'Lilith' (NRSV, not verified) turns the class noun into a personal name and brings in the later figure of the Talmud (long hair, b. ʿErub. 100b; wings, b. Nid. 24b; seizing sleepers, b. Šabb. 151b; recalled) and of the medieval Alphabet of Ben Sira, where Lilith is Adam's first wife (B. Hutter, 'Lilith', DDD, 2nd ed., 1999; recalled); that figure is reception history and is kept to commentary. The KJV 'screech owl' takes lîlîṯ as a bird (KJV renders śāʿîr in the same verse 'the satyr', so it does not take every creature as an animal); the Akkadian evidence does not support a bird for this word, and the reading is recorded in commentary. The entry is direct: 'the night-monster' is the public-domain baseline and agrees with the lexical consensus that lîlîṯ is a demon; the staged 'the lilith' would also be direct (NJPS). The wave I-5 rulings require the word to be rendered by philology and the lens-salient reading of Lilith to stay out of the line; the line encodes neither the later personal figure nor any project reading, and the one labelled speculative paragraph at 34:14 states that the Raëlian canon texts in data-library neither cite the verse nor name Lilith.

entry.lemma: the creatures that occupy a ruined city in Isaiah's judgment oracles
entry.partOfSpeech: nouns (animal and bird names), mostly plural
entry.literal: desert-dwellers; howlers; jackals; daughters of the ostrich; (an unclean bird); (a hedgehog-like animal or a bird); (a bird, owl?); (a nesting creature, snake or owl?); kites
entry.standardEnglish: 34:11 ASV 'the pelican and the porcupine … the owl'; JPS 1917 'the pelican and the bittern … the owl'; NJPS 'Jackdaws and owls … Great owls' (note: meaning uncertain). 34:13 ASV 'jackals … ostriches'; JPS 1917 'wild-dogs … ostriches'; NJPS 'jackals … ostriches'. 34:14 ASV 'the wild beasts of the desert … the wolves'; JPS 1917 'the wild-cats … the jackals'; NJPS 'Wildcats … hyenas'. 34:15 ASV 'the dart-snake … the kites'; JPS 1917 'the arrowsnake … the kites'; NJPS 'the arrow-snake … the buzzards'. All checked 2026-11-26 (ASV bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS Sefaria).
entry.wohChoice: One English name per Hebrew creature name across Isaiah's ruin passages: ṣiyyîm 'desert creatures' and ʾiyyîm 'hyenas' (as at 13:21-22); tannîm 'jackals' (as at 13:22; 35:7; 43:20; distinct from tannîn 'dragon', central taninim); bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh 'ostriches' (13:21; 43:20); qāʾaṯ 'pelican'; qippōḏ 'porcupine' (as at 14:23); yanšôp̄ 'owl'; qippôz 'dart-snake'; dayyôṯ 'kites'. ʿōrēḇ 'raven' is governed by central yonah-orev, śāʿîr 'wild goat' by lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah, and lîlîṯ by lilit-night-monster-isaiah-34.
entry.rationale: Isaiah describes the ruin of a city by listing the creatures that move into it, at 13:21-22, 14:23 and 34:11-15 (cf. Zeph 2:14; Jer 50:39), and several names recur across these passages. Most of the identifications are uncertain (NJPS notes at 34:11 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain' and at 34:14 that most of the creatures in vv. 14-15 'cannot be identified with certainty'), so no rendering can claim to be the right animal. What the translation can do is give each Hebrew name one English name wherever it recurs, so that the reader of 34:11-15 recognises the creatures of 13:21-22 and 14:23. The stable chapters fix ṣiyyîm 'desert creatures', ʾiyyîm 'hyenas' (NRSV), tannîm 'jackals', bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh 'ostriches' and qippōḏ 'porcupine', and this entry applies them at 34:11-14. Where the book has no earlier decision, the ASV names are kept (qāʾaṯ 'pelican', yanšôp̄ 'owl', qippôz 'dart-snake', dayyôṯ 'kites'); the alternatives of JPS 1917 and NJPS are given in commentary. qippōḏ is the hardest case: in the bird list of 34:11 a bird is likely (JPS 1917 'bittern', NJPS 'owls'), and Zeph 2:14, where qāʾaṯ and qippōḏ lodge on the capitals of columns, points the same way, but ASV's 'porcupine' is kept for concordance with 14:23; if a later pass changes it, both sites change together. tannîm 'jackals' is a different word from tannîn 'dragon, sea monster' (27:1), and the central taninim entry is not applied. The entry is direct: each rendering is that of ASV or of the stable chapters, which follow ASV or NRSV. The orchestrator may add ISA-13:21, ISA-13:22, ISA-14:23 and ISA-43:20 to appliesTo with no change to those lines, and the chapter-35 Editor may add ISA-35:7 (tannîm 'jackals').

entry.strongs: H4393 (mᵉlōʾ); H6631 (ṣeʾĕṣāʾîm); H4549 (māsas); H4743 (māqaq); H5034 (nāḇēl); H2719 (ḥereḇ); H2715 (ḥōr); H4410 (mᵉlûḵāh); H2681 (ḥāṣîr 'court, enclosure'). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: lexical and syntactic cruxes of Isaiah 34
entry.partOfSpeech: nouns; Niphal and Qal verbs; nominal clause
entry.literal: its fullness … its offspring; they shall melt; they shall rot … it shall wither as the withering of … and as a withering (one); a sword belongs to YHWH; its nobles … they shall call; enclosure
entry.standardEnglish: 34:1 ASV and JPS 1917 'the fulness thereof … all things that come forth (of/from) it'; NJPS 'those in it … what it brings forth'. 34:3 ASV and JPS 1917 'the mountains shall be melted with their blood'; NJPS 'the hills shall be drenched with their blood'. 34:4 ASV 'shall be dissolved … fade away … as a fading [leaf]'; JPS 1917 'moulder away … fall down … a falling fig'; NJPS 'molder … wither … shriveled fruit'. 34:6 ASV and JPS 1917 'The sword of Jehovah/the LORD is filled with blood'; NJPS 'The LORD has a sword; it is sated with blood'. 34:12 ASV 'They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there'; JPS 1917 'As for her nobles, none shall be there to be called to the kingdom'; NJPS 'It shall be called, "No kingdom is there"' (note: meaning uncertain). 34:13 ASV 'a court'; JPS 1917 'an enclosure'; NJPS 'an abode'. All checked 2026-11-26.
entry.wohChoice: 34:1 ûmᵉlōʾāh 'and its fullness', ṣeʾĕṣāʾeyhā 'all that comes forth from it' (ASV). 34:3 nāmassû 'shall be melted' (ASV, JPS 1917). 34:4 nāmaqqû 'shall rot away' (line change from the draft's ASV 'shall be dissolved'); nbl 'fade' throughout the verse ('shall fade away, as the leaf fades from the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig tree'), with 'leaf' supplied as in ASV. 34:6 ḥereḇ laYHWH 'The sword of YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917). 34:12 ASV kept: 'Its nobles they shall call to the kingdom, but none shall be there'. 34:13 ḥāṣîr 'a court' (ASV).
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the Translator asked whether to keep the ASV or follow a modern version, and the entry records the decision so that the English line is backed by the glossary. The one line change is at 34:4. The verb mqq means 'rot, fester, waste away' (BDB; HALOT; recalled): wounds fester (Ps 38:6), flesh rots (Zech 14:12), and the noun maq is 'rottenness' at Isa 3:24 and 5:24 in this translation. ASV's 'shall be dissolved' gives the result without the image, while JPS 1917 'moulder away' and NJPS 'molder' keep the decay; 'shall rot away' keeps the root's sense and its English family in the book. In the same verse nbl is 'fade', as ASV has it and as the book has it at 40:7-8 ('the flower fades'); the participle nōḇeleṯ has no noun, and 'leaf' is supplied with ASV rather than JPS 1917 'fig' or NJPS 'fruit'. The other items keep ASV: at 34:3 the literal 'melted' over NJPS's paraphrase 'drenched'; at 34:6 the genitive construal 'The sword of YHWH' (ASV, JPS 1917) over NJPS's possessive nominal clause, a difference of syntax and not of sense; at 34:12, a crux (NJPS 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'), the ASV construal, which needs no emendation, with the readings of JPS 1917 and NJPS and the proposal that a word has fallen out given in commentary; at 34:13 ḥāṣîr is the 'enclosure, abode' noun related to ḥāṣēr 'court' and not ḥāṣîr 'grass', and ASV's 'a court' gives that sense. At 34:1 mᵉlōʾāh 'its fullness' (ASV, JPS 1917) keeps the noun, where NJPS paraphrases 'those in it'. None of the choices carries a lens.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-5, chapter 34: the descriptive title is 'Isaiah 34 — Judgment on the nations and on Edom: the host of the heavens rots away, the sword in Bozrah, and the creatures of the ruin'; the draft's 'dissolved' was changed with the 34:4 line (lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34).

Wave I-5: at 34:1 hā-ʾāreṣ ûmᵉlōʾāh stands in parallel with tēḇēl 'the world' in a summons to all nations and peoples, and is 'the earth'. The territorial ʾereṣ of 34:6, 7, 9 (Edom's land) stays 'land' under the central eretz entry.

Wave I-5 extension: at 34:4 kas-sēp̄er 'like a scroll' (the sky rolled up like a written roll; ASV 'as a scroll', NJPS 'like a scroll') and at 34:16 sēp̄er YHWH 'the scroll of YHWH' (NJPS 'the scroll of the LORD'; ASV and JPS 1917 'the book'). The same noun is rendered the same way in both verses of the chapter, and the line does not say which scroll is meant at 34:16; the proposals (a written collection of prophecy, cf. 30:8; a divine register, cf. Exod 32:32-33) are in commentary. The chapter-30 Editor should check 30:8 (bᵉsēp̄er, draft 'in a book') against this entry.

Wave I-5: the measuring-line clause applied at 34:11 (qaw-tōhû 'the line of wasteland', with ʾaḇnê-ḇōhû 'the plummet of emptiness') and 34:17 (baq-qāw 'by line'), as the wohChoice provides. The reduplicated forms at 28:10, 13 are left to the chapter-28 Editor.

Wave I-5 extension: at 34:14 the singular (collective) wᵉśāʿîr ʿal-rēʿēhû yiqrāʾ is 'the wild goat shall cry to its fellow' (ASV), following the 13:21 decision; JPS 1917 has 'the satyr' and NJPS 'Goat-demons shall greet each other' (checked 2026-11-26). The corpus prints 'goat-demons' for the same noun at LEV-WOH-17:7 (leviticus-woh overlay seirim-goat-demons-leviticus-17-7), where the śᵉʿîrîm receive sacrifices and must be beings that can be worshipped; in Isaiah's lists of creatures in a ruin that condition is absent, so the corpus renders one noun two ways by context. The difference is deliberate and recorded. At 34:14 the neighbouring lîlîṯ (lilit-night-monster-isaiah-34), a demon by philology, makes the demonic reading stronger than at 13:21, and the choice is flagged for founder review. PENDING FOUNDER RULING, staged alternative: 'goat-demon(s)' at both sites, with the lines 34:14 'and the goat-demon shall cry to its fellow' and 13:21 (stable, chapter 13 version bump) 'and goat-demons will dance there', and this entry's wohChoice item '13:21 śᵉʿîrîm wild goats (ASV kept; goat-demons in commentary)' changed to '13:21 śᵉʿîrîm goat-demons; 34:14 śāʿîr the goat-demon (NJPS; as LEV-WOH-17:7)' (a wohChoice modification, major bump). Until the ruling the lines keep 'wild goats' / 'the wild goat'.

Wave I-5: at 34:16 wᵉrûḥô hûʾ qibbᵉṣān 'and his spirit, it has gathered them' takes lower-case 'spirit' (NJPS 'His spirit'; ASV 'his Spirit'). JPS 1917 refers the suffix to the mouth, 'the breath thereof' (cf. Ps 33:6), and that reading is recorded in commentary.

Wave I-5, chapter 34: MT translated and variants reported in commentary at 34:4 (1QIsaᵃ 'And the valleys shall be cleft, / And all the host of heaven shall wither', from the NJPS note), 34:5 (1QIsaᵃ 'be seen' for riwwᵉṯāh, cf. Targum, from the NJPS note), 34:7 (emendation 'with fatted calves', from the NJPS note) and 34:16 (MT 'my mouth'; NJPS emends to 'His'; a 1QIsaᵃ 'his mouth' is reported in the literature, not checked). None of the scroll readings was checked against the scroll or a DJD edition. The orchestrator may add these to the wohChoice variant list on merge.
